key_insight: CAFM reframes EHR foundation models around patient cohorts as the primary unit of evidence, aiming to improve interpretability, robustness, and clinical alignment.
clinical_relevance: By making cohort comparisons explicit and auditable, the framework could support more trustworthy risk prediction and multimodal clinical decision support across EHR use cases.
method: Deviation-aware data curation to improve training data quality
Cohort-conditioned pretraining plus multimodal cohort alignment
evidence_signal: The abstract presents four clinical case studies and five empirically testable hypotheses, but it does not report new performance results in this paper.
watch_item: The approach remains a framework proposal, so its real-world value depends on validation under distribution shift, irregular temporality, and cross-modal data quality constraints.
paper_title: Cohort-Anchored Foundation Models for Electronic Health Records: From Risk Scores to Auditable Peer Cohorts
